summary.summary: PARTIAL on the response inside a halo: the first-order drift of a free test record in a gas with density gradient g is exactly g(18c^3 pqr - 10c^2 pq + 11c^2 pr + 11c^2 qr - 17cp - 17cq + 4cr - 24)/(3(cp+1)(cq+1)(cr+1)), of which the blocking of occupied targets contributes exactly -1 independently of c, p, q and r.  At the neutral scale this is NEGATIVE on every triple tested - -26/45 sort of magnitudes, specifically the coefficient is negative at (3,1,2), (12,1,2), (5,2,4) and (7,3,5) - so contrary to the unit's expectation a single test record does NOT have zero drift at the neutral scale: it drifts AWAY from density.  Both causes survive at c_0: blocking, and the concavity of phi/(1+phi), which makes <phi/(1+phi)> < 1/2 even though <c_0 omega> = 1.  The drift reverses to up-gradient only above a scale c* which is 1.38 to 2.09 times c_0 on the triples tested.  A held cube of side m instead drifts up the gradient at kappa g m / 2, linear in the side; combined with the halo u = QG/kappa this gives v_B = Q_A m_B/(8 pi R^2), one over R squared, linear in A's production and in B's linear size, hence NOT symmetric under exchanging A and B

what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 5: What a second lump does inside a halo: drift up a density gradient. SETTING (blocks 39, 40, 41; open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move', 'ail40', 'ail41: what a source is'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record (content = one of the six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal contents), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; the neutral scale is c_0 = 6/(p+q+4r), at which every row of W sums to 6 and records do not bind on any window without a cycle (all binding is the loop factor 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n, l_1 = (p-q)/(p+q+4r), l_2 = (p+q-2r)/(p+q+4r)). Motion: a record hops to an empty neighbour, choosing between its two positions in proportion to the pair weights it would have there (an isolated record hops symmetrically). Formation: an empty site x forms a record at rate z Z_x, Z_x = sum over contents a of the product of W(a, s_y) over the recorded neighbours y, content drawn in proportion to the summand; records are never removed. BLOCK 41 PROVED: (1) the only local additive invariant density is the occupancy: mass = number of records; (2) two sets of records separated by empty sites weigh the product of their weights, at any scale: no action across empty sites; (3) the field of a held record through a medium is the pair correlation, of short range (ladder exact; cubic lattice about one step or less away from the clumping onset); (4) the content field around a record is a number times its content vector, zero for a record of unread content: the mass has no charge in the long-range tilt channel; (5) under symmetric hops with one record per site d<n_x>/dt = kappa * (lattice Laplacian of <n>)_x + j_x exactly, j the mean formation rate, so a steady excess of production carries the stationary halo G * (j - mean j)/kappa with G the lattice Green function (one-over-distance on Z^3); at the neutral scale the formation rate next to ONE record is exactly the void's (Z_x = 6), next to records of independent uniform contents it is the void's on average, and next to k agreeing records it is larger by 6^(k-1) (p^k+q^k+4r^k)/(p+q+4r)^k (13/12, 5/4 at (3,1,2); 46/21, 2348/343 at (12,1,2); k = 2, 3). NOT YET KNOWN: what a lump's halo looks like, how strong it is, and what a second lump does inside it. TASK: block 41 found a field (the halo of free records around a producing lump) but no force law. Derive the response. (a) A test record at scale c > c_0, or a small bound cluster whose binding comes from loops at c_0, sits in a gas of free records whose mean density has a small uniform gradient g along x. Using pair-weight motion, derive the mean drift velocity of the test object to first order in g and in the gas density: its sign (towards higher density?), and its dependence on c/c_0, on the loop factors, and on the object's record count. State exactly what is assumed about the gas (independent sites at density rho(x)). (b) Show that at the neutral scale a single test record has zero drift at this order (it binds to nothing without a cycle) and find the lowest order at which a drift appears. (c) Accretion: a held lump in a gradient gains records faster on the high-density side; compute the rate of displacement of its centre of mass to first order in g for a cube of side m. (d) Combine with the halo u = Q G/kappa: the velocity of object B at distance R from producer A, its dependence on Q_A, on B's record count, on R (one over R squared?), and whether the law is symmetric under exchanging A and B. An overdamped velocity law is not a force law with inertia: say so and say what would be needed for one. check.py: exact first-order drift on a small periodic window by enumeration of the gas configurations around the test object.
